name: Diffie–Hellman
role: Key agreement without a shared secret: the birth of public-key cryptography.
source: Diffie & Hellman, New Directions in Cryptography

name: RSA
role: Encryption and signatures whose security rests on factoring large integers.

name: Elliptic-curve cryptography
role: Discrete logarithms on elliptic curves: RSA-level security with much smaller keys.

name: SEC 2 publishes secp256k1
role: The curve y² = x³ + 7 that Bitcoin and Ethereum later chose, with its G and n.

name: SHA-2
role: NIST's SHA-256/SHA-512 family (Merkle–Damgård); still unbroken, used by BIP-39 and BIP-32.

name: Bitcoin white paper
role: secp256k1 + ECDSA + SHA-256 in a public ledger; the network went live in January 2009.
source: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System

name: BIP-32
role: Hierarchical deterministic wallets: one seed, an unlimited tree of keys.

name: Keccak wins the SHA-3 competition
role: A sponge design, structurally unlike SHA-2, chosen as insurance in case SHA-2 fell.

name: BIP-39
role: Backup words with a checksum, and the PBKDF2 seed derived from them.

name: BIP-44
role: Standard paths m/purpose'/coin'/account'/change/index, so wallets find the same keys.

name: Ethereum launch
role: Keccak-256 addresses, smart contracts, and the original Keccak padding fixed in the protocol.

name: SHA-3 = FIPS 202
role: Keccak standardised with a different padding byte: SHA3-256 ≠ Ethereum's Keccak-256.

name: EIP-55
role: A typo-detecting checksum hidden in the letter case of the hex address.

name: FIPS 203/204/205
role: Post-quantum standards: lattice-based ML-KEM and ML-DSA, hash-based SLH-DSA.

name: Coldcard entropy failure
role: Seeds from a timer-seeded PRNG since 2021: valid words, guessable entropy, wallets swept.
